html:
The Battle of Santa Clara was fought in the last days of December 1958 in the city of Santa Clara in central Cuba. Rebels led by Che Guevara took the city from the army of the dictator Fulgencio Batista, who fled the country hours later.

Fidel Castro's rebels had fought from the mountains of eastern Cuba since 1956; see the Cuban Revolution. After Batista's big offensive failed in the summer of 1958, Castro sent Guevara west with a small column to cut the island in two. Santa Clara was held by over 3,000 soldiers with tanks. Guevara had about 340 fighters. Batista sent an armoured train with fresh troops and weapons. The rebels tore up the track with a bulldozer, and the train ran off the rails. Its men gave up after a short fight against petrol bombs. With the help of townspeople the rebels then took the barracks and police station one by one.

Batista flew out of Havana in the first hours of 1 January 1959. Guevara's men entered the capital the next day, and Castro a week later. Cuba became a communist state allied to the Soviet Union, 150 km from the United States.
